scope: Exploratory fixed-volume constant-speed thermal-conversion diagnostic, not a blind validation or official FIRAS likelihood.
data_selection: All released numeric rows; use residual column 3, uncertainty column 4 and Galaxy-template column 5. Do not fit the rounded reconstructed column 2.
conversion_rule: Every photon energy scales by q, photon number and physical volume fixed, constant vacuum c and standard density of modes. An initial exact blackbody becomes q^-3 times a Planck spectrum at the fitted final color temperature.
nuisances: Final color temperature in [0.5,4] K and an unconstrained signed coefficient for the released Galaxy residual template. No freely fitted blackbody amplitude in the fixed-q hypotheses.
comparator: Additional descriptive fit with positive free blackbody amplitude, free color temperature in [0.5,4] K, and the same Galaxy template.
objective: Sum squared residuals divided by the published diagonal variances. No covariance, instrument gain prior or full foreground model supplied.
interpretation: Report diagnostic chi-square and residuals, not exclusion significance, a confidence interval, a cosmic age, or an inferred absolute conversion rate. Initial thermal conditions are an explicit conditional premise. Escape, photon absorption/emission and thermalization are omitted, not ruled out.
